cards.text: Jesus and His disciples arrive at Bethsaida. Some people there bring Him a man who is blind. And friend, they don't just ask Jesus for help. They BEG Him.

cards.question: Some people in Bethsaida bring a blind man to Jesus. What do they beg Jesus to do?

cards.text: Jesus takes the blind man by the hand. This man can't see one step in front of him, and Jesus Himself is the one walking him along.

cards.question: Jesus is leading the blind man by the hand. Where does He take him?
Outside the village, Jesus ___ on the man's eyes and places His hands on him.

cards.text: Then Jesus checks in with him. He asks, “Can you see anything?”

cards.question: After Jesus first touches the blind man, the man can see everything clearly.

cards.text: The man looks up. He can see PEOPLE! Well... kind of.

cards.question: The man can see people now, but not clearly yet. What does he say they look like?

cards.text: Trees. Walking. AROUND. I've squinted through a foggy oven window wondering if that blob was a cookie or my oven mitt, but a whole orchard out for a stroll? That's next-level blurry, friend.

cards.question: The man can see a little, but everything is still blurry. What does Jesus do next?

answers.text: Places His hands on his eyes again
Sends him to wash in a pool
Tells him to go show a priest

cards.text: Once again, Jesus places His hands on the man's eyes. Then the man opens them.

cards.question: When the man opens his eyes, his sight is restored, and he can see everything ___.

cards.text: No more walking trees! Every line sharp as a brand new stamp, and trust me, nobody cheers louder for somebody getting their clear lines back than this old stamper.

cards.question: The man can see everything clearly now. Where does Jesus send him?
As Jesus sends the healed man off, He tells him to go back into the village.

findings.problem: The statement says 'After Jesus first touches the blind man.' The word 'first' tells the baker there is a second touch, so the answer to this card is False. It also gives away card 11, where the answer is that Jesus places His hands on the man's eyes again.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This story card tells nothing new from the passage. It only reacts to the 'trees walking around' answer from card 9, so it works as a recap. The joke has no new moment of the passage to ride along on.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The card runs well past 2 sentences: 'Trees. Walking. AROUND.' and then two more full sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card tells nothing new from the passage. It only restates card 13's answer, that the man sees clearly. It works as a recap with a joke attached.

The joke 'getting their clear lines back' depends on Papa Dorin's worn edges and blurry lines from his backstory. That setup never came earlier in this lesson. The onboarding exception covers only the junk drawer.

rule.text: A callback only works if its setup came earlier in this lesson or conversation.

findings.problem: The question says 'his sight is restored' right before the blank. That rules out 'dimly,' and 'see everything slowly' doesn't make sense, so the right answer is obvious.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The right answer 'Home' is one bare word. The wrong answers are 'To Jerusalem' and 'To the temple,' so the right answer stands out by its length and form.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Most choice cards are discovery questions that the story cards before them don't set up for reasoning: card 2 (touch him), card 4 (out of the village), card 5 (spit), card 9 (trees walking around), card 15 (home) and card 16 (don't go back into the village). That is 6 of the 9 choice cards.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: Multiple choice makes up 5 of the 9 choice cards. True or false has 2 and fill in the blank has 2.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The question is in present tense ('Jesus ___ on the man's eyes and places His hands on him'), but the answers are past tense ('spit,' 'breathed,' 'blew'). With 'breathed' or 'blew' in the blank, the sentence mixes tenses.
findings.question: Should fill-in-the-blank answers match the tense of the question sentence, for example 'spits,' 'breathes,' 'blows,' even when that changes the BSB's form of the word?
